plan.title: Entropy: why a hot coffee never reheats itself
plan.description: Entropy measures how spread out energy is, and why the second law makes some processes irreversible. The same idea, in Claude Shannon's information theory, measures uncertainty.

beats.narration: Why does a hot coffee always cool down, but never heats itself back up? The answer is one idea: entropy.

props.alt: hot coffee cooling in a mug

beats.narration: Entropy measures how spread out energy is. Low entropy means energy is concentrated in one place. High entropy means it is dispersed evenly. Left alone, energy spreads out.

This is the second law of thermodynamics. The entropy of an isolated system cannot decrease with time. So systems drift toward equilibrium, where entropy is highest. That is why some processes are irreversible.
Entropy also measures uncertainty. In 1948, Claude Shannon used it to describe information. The more unpredictable a message, the more information it carries. It is measured in bits.

steps.note: Average uncertainty, in bits with log base 2

beats.narration: Entropy is how many ways things can be arranged, and nature drifts toward the most likely arrangement. Hot coffee cools because spread-out energy is overwhelmingly more probable.

props.text: Nature drifts toward the most likely arrangement.
